events.ai_basis: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> (on commit 2725d47 'Unconditional (5,5,23) proof: generators, docs, CI' and on 4b7455f reimplementing Stoll's criterion)

why: Pre-2024 signature results are cases digested by publication; Norvig's search is instances; Mihailescu/Bartolome papers concern the factored norm equation, a variant. All full-proof claims (Daras, Bado, Ben Hadj Salem, Vega x2, Preprints.org x2, Hanners, Aabidi, Harris, Davlatov) are scoped whole but set aside as not_credible: each combines no uptake on a prize problem, non-standard or elementary methods the problem resists, and version churn or self-contradiction. Zhou I/II claim many signatures via IUT; I set them not_credible because the method rests on the step the community considers broken, plus the dubious citation bookkeeping, rather than merely doubtful. The Anthropic FLT post formalises a known proof (none; Buzzard's review digests the formal artefact). The beals repository settles one signature (5,5,23) unconditionally where only a GRH-conditional result existed, so it is a case; it is unreviewed and doubtful but has a concrete, reproducible method and no identified error. Its AI role is the closest call: the only basis is a commit co-author trailer, but that trailer sits on the commits that produce the load-bearing reimplementation of Stoll's criterion and the certification that constitutes the proof, which is part of the result, so assisted rather than none; generated is not supported since the human chose the reduction from cited work.
doubts: The beals AI role rests on commit trailers alone; the README and write-up say nothing about what Claude produced, so 'assisted' could be 'none' (if Claude only wrote tests/CI) or stronger. Its novelty may be pre-empted by a Bartolome-Mihailescu claim the record could not locate. Zhou's not_credible call versus doubtful is a judgement on the IUT dispute's standing. Devpost event is snippet-only and its AI role unknown.
